# docs — agent guide

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
The verifiably ecosystem's front door: its goal, overview, and repository map
<!-- ops:identity end -->

## Gates

`just check` runs ops-check, ops-docs check, the link checker, and `tasks check`; the
pre-commit hook runs it. `just test` runs the link checker alone. The link checker
verifies `https://github.com/verifiably/<repo>/blob/main/<path>` links against the
sibling checkout `../<repo>` and reports a sibling that is absent rather than passing
it. On a fresh clone, run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once.

## Layout

- `overview.md` — the ecosystem overview; `README.md` — the repository map.
- `family.toml` — the family declaration; `tools/ops-docs family check` at pre-push
  judges every member's committed copy against it.
- `templates/README.md` — the member README template; `tools/check_links.py` skips
  `templates/`.
- `tools/check_links.py` — this repository's own link checker.
- `tools/tt`, `tools/ops-check`, `tools/ops-docs` — vendored from ops; update from there.

## Rules

- Ecosystem level only. A repository's own mechanics belong in that repository's
  guide, beside the designs they summarize, so a design change updates them in the same
  commit; here, link to them. Restating kernel detail here is how it drifts.
- Link across repositories with `https://github.com/verifiably/<repo>/blob/main/<path>`,
  never a relative `../<repo>` path, which breaks on GitHub; the link checker verifies
  only the first form.
- Lead with the goal, not the machinery: understanding the world from small,
  reproducible analyses. Reproduction, belief computation and specs serve that goal and
  are described as such.
- A state claim names its authority. The overview's layer-state column is a dated
  snapshot; when a layer's state changes, update it or the date.
- A member's label in `family.toml` is the layer column of the README table; a change
  to one is a change to both, and nothing checks it.
